t: A kingdom of the Yemeni highlands, ruled from Zafar, that united all of south Arabia around 300 CE.
Around 380 its kings gave up the old gods for one god, the Merciful, in a monotheism close to Judaism.
Conflict with Christian Najran and Aksum ended in Kaleb’s invasion of 525, in which the last king, Yusuf, was killed.
dyk: The Himyarites dated their inscriptions by their own era, which began around 110 BCE, so many Himyarite texts can be dated to the exact year.
ev: The Himyarite era, later used to date inscriptions, begins
A Roman expedition under Aelius Gallus reaches south Arabia and withdraws
Shammar Yuhar'ish annexes the Kingdom of Saba
Himyar annexes the Kingdom of Hadramawt and unites south Arabia
The royal court abandons the old gods for monotheism
Sharahbil Ya'fur records major repairs of the Marib Dam
Yusuf As'ar Yath'ar besieges Najran, where many Christians are killed
Kaleb of Aksum invades, and Yusuf is defeated and killed
